# The negation of a round-up interval

<!-- Generated by docs/tools/reference.py from gen/claims.json, gen/kernels/, include/kairn/gen/, proofs/gen/, proofs/audit/, results/*/brute/, results/brute-code.json and docs/tools/reference_operations.py. Do not edit: run python3 docs/tools/reference.py. -->

Kernel `upward_neg_1` · **UNVERIFIED** · [all operations](index.md) · [how to read this page](reading.md)

A kernel of the round-up interval ([its kernels](upward.md)), of the opt-in header `kairn/upward.hpp`, which `kairn/kairn.hpp` does not include and which requires the options of [The round-up interval](../concepts/upward.md) (GCC and Clang `-frounding-math`, MSVC `/fp:strict`). No operation of it rounds: it gives the same result in every rounding mode.

**UNVERIFIED: no proof is checked.** The statement below is a target: Rocq has not checked a proof of it. No public operation calls it yet ([What holds today](../getting-started/guarantees.md#proved-and-unverified)).

## What it computes

A state of the round-up interval $Z = [-z_n, z_u]$ that contains $-x$ for every $x \in X$, with $X = [-x_n, x_u]$. An interval may be unbounded, and empty.

$$Z \supseteq \{\, -x : x \in X \,\}.$$

A state of the round-up interval is stored as its upper bound and its lower bound negated, the two lanes of one register: $X$ as $(x_u, x_n)$, $Z$ as $(z_u, z_n)$ ([its kernels](upward.md#the-stored-pair)).

## C++

**Not yet called by the public headers.** No public operation computes this kernel yet.

## Requires

- $X = [-x_n, x_u]$, stored as $(x_u, x_n)$, is a canonical state of the round-up interval: the empty set, both lanes a NaN; or a nonempty interval, each lane a number of `T` or $+\infty$ (neither a NaN nor $-\infty$), with $-x_n \le x_u$; its members are the real numbers between $-x_n$ and $x_u$.

## Target (not proved)

For operands that satisfy the requirements, finite, infinite or NaN:

- **I1.** The result $Z = [-z_n, z_u]$, stored as $(z_u, z_n)$, is a canonical state of the round-up interval.
- **I2.** $Z$ is empty exactly when $X$ is.
- **I3.** $Z$ contains $-x$ for every $x \in X$, unbounded operands included (their members are real numbers).
- **I4.** For nonempty $X$, where $\ell$ and $h$ are the greatest lower bound and the least upper bound of the exact range $\{\, -x : x \in X \,\}$, as extended real numbers: $-z_n = \ell$ and $z_u = h$, exactly.
- **I5.** For bounded $X$, $Z$ is bounded exactly when every member $z$ of the exact range satisfies $\lvert z\rvert \le \Omega$.

Stated for every binary format with a precision of at least 1 bit, no operation of the kernel rounding, in the IEEE model, with signed zeros, infinities, NaN and overflow. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/upward_neg_1.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/upward_neg_1.kernel), the description the C++ (`include/kairn/gen/upward.hpp`) and the formal model (`proofs/gen/UpwardModel.v`) are generated from. Each statement is one operation of `T`, and none rounds to nearest ([the round-up interval in the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-round-up-interval)). A line of two statements separated by ` | ` is a *pair line*: the two lanes of one instruction, lane 0 on the left ([the pair form](../developer/design/upward.md#the-pair-form)).

```
# The negation of an interval of the round-up interval (docs/developer/design/upward.md, "Sum,
# difference, negation"): the two lanes exchanged, -[a, b] = [-b, -a] stored as (a, -b); exact, in
# every rounding mode; the empty set stays empty. Requires the rounding mode upward set by
# kairn::upward::Scope and the options of docs/concepts/upward.md (GCC and Clang -frounding-math,
# MSVC /fp:strict).

zu = copy(xn) | zn = copy(xu)                   # swap(x)
```
